facts.statement: Urbacodon is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur.
facts.quote: Urbacodon (meaning "URBAC tooth") is a genus of troodontid theropod dinosaur.

facts.statement: Two species of Urbacodon are known only from partial lower jaws.
facts.quote: Two species have been described, both of which are known from a partial dentary

facts.statement: A lower jaw of Urbacodon was uncovered on September 9, 2004, near Itemir in Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: On 9 September 2004, a lower jaw of a small theropod was uncovered by Anton Sergeevich Rezwiy near Itemir in the IT-01 quarry near Dzharakuduk.

facts.statement: The type species Urbacodon itemirensis was named by Averianov and Sues in 2007.
facts.quote: The type species, Urbacodon itemirensis, was named by Alexandr Averianov and Hans-Dieter Sues in 2007.

facts.statement: The genus name Urbacodon is an acronym honoring scientists from Uzbekistan, Russia, Britain, America, and Canada.
facts.quote: The first part of the generic name Urbacodon is an acronym, honouring the Uzbek, Russian, British, American and Canadian scientists who participated in its discovery.

facts.statement: The holotype of Urbacodon itemirensis is a single left lower jaw with replacement teeth from the Cenomanian Dzharakuduk Formation.
facts.quote: The name was based on the holotype ZIN PH 944/16, a single left dentary with preserved replacement teeth from the Cenomanian Dzharakuduk Formation.

facts.statement: A second species, Urbacodon norelli, was described in 2024 based on a partial right lower jaw collected in the late 1990s.
facts.quote: In 2024, Wang et al. described a partial right dentary collected from the Iren Dabasu Formation in the late 1990s.

facts.statement: The holotype lower jaw of U. itemirensis is 79.2 mm long and contains 32 tooth positions.
facts.quote: The holotype dentary of U. itemirensis is 79.2 mm long and has 32 tooth positions.

facts.statement: A distinctive gap between the front and rear teeth exists in the holotype, though it may represent individual variation rather than a unique trait.
facts.quote: This is a unique trait but was not formally designated as an autapomorphy because it might be the result of individual variation.

facts.statement: Urbacodon differs from Mei by being considerably larger and from Byronosaurus by having less vascularized lateral grooves and more bulbous front teeth.
facts.quote: Urbacodon is distinguished from Byronosaurus by a less vascularized lateral dentary groove and more bulbous anterior tooth crowns, and from Mei by considerably larger size.

facts.statement: Unlike most other troodontids, Urbacodon teeth lack serrations.
facts.quote: Urbacodon resembles Byronosaurus and Mei but differs from most other Troodontidae in that its teeth lack serrations.

facts.statement: A 2010 cladistic analysis identified Urbacodon as a close relative of Byronosaurus and Xixiasaurus.
facts.quote: In 2010, a cladistic analysis showed it as a close relative of Byronosaurus and Xixiasaurus.

facts.statement: Urbacodon fossils are found in the Cenomanian Dzharakuduk Formation of Uzbekistan and the Iren Dabasu Formation of China.
facts.quote: U. itemirensis from the Dzharakuduk Formation (Cenomanian) of Uzbekistan and U. norelli from the Iren Dabasu Formation of China.

facts.statement: Urbacodon lived during the mid-Cretaceous, approximately 95 to 90 million years ago, in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivieron a mediados del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente entre 95 y 90 millones de años, desde el Cenomaniense al Turoniense, en lo que es hoy Asia.

facts.statement: Possible remains of Urbacodon are known from the Turonian Bissekty Formation of Uzbekistan.
facts.quote: Possible remains are also known from the Bissekty Formation (Turonian) of Uzbekistan.

facts.statement: Both Urbacodon specimens share a lightweight, strap-like lower jaw that curves inward at the tip, a symphyseal foramen, and thickened dentary teeth.
facts.quote: Los dos especímenes comparten un dentario de estructura ligera y con forma de correa que se curva hacia adentro en la punta, un foramen sinfisario en el dentario y dientes dentarios engrosados, entre otras características.

facts.statement: It is debated whether the distinctive gap between the front and rear teeth is a unique trait or merely individual variation.
facts.quote: This is a unique trait but was not formally designated as an autapomorphy because it might be the result of individual variation.

rejected.statement: A 2024 analysis recovered Zanabazar as the sister taxon to Urbacodon within the Troodontidae.
rejected.quote: They recovered Zanabazar as the sister taxon to Urbacodon as late-diverging members of the Troodontidae.
